title: Retro game remakes and native application discovery
summary: Add fourteen qualified projects after reviewing 32 roots; record eighteen deferrals and duplicate-adjacent cases.
notes: Root personally searched all six requested platform families and reviewed 32 pinned roots. Fourteen qualified game/reconstruction/application entries and eighteen deferrals or duplicate-adjacent cases. No discovery worker used. Separate original-author remakes, source preservation, subsystem research and unfinished engines; do not infer fidelity from screenshots or a README claim. No upstream software executed. Pinned bytes are ephemeral local review material only; retained submission carries immutable proof identities without source excerpts.

sources.reason: From-scratch replacement for the unavailable full ClassMate GUI builder, updated for ReAction. Inspected E source generates C declarations and ReAction calls, with multi-window layouts, menu preview and gadget objects. This is a functional reimplementation, not recovered ClassMate source.

Independent OpenGL remake with its own game library, arena, enemies, bombs, navigation and level script. Author explicitly states most features are implemented but only the first level is designed. Not a full-game restoration.

Semantic Lua remake with bomb movement, timed and remote detonation, fireballs, player/item/block entities and shop/standings scenes. Enhanced presentation is intentional. README contains generic placeholder clone/run instructions, so use the inspected makefile for the actual game root.

Memory-based recreation of the Amiga typing game with mission selection, home-row lessons, shield/target states and pilot profiles. Author explicitly calls the curriculum unfinished; practice, scoring history and some audio controls remain TODO. Inspected state-name table has fewer entries than state enum, so do not equate source presence with robust runtime completion.

Repository contains DOS-oriented C functions, assembly listings, executable/file maps and anti-debug research. Inspected game code names chest-key checks and status output but retains a commented unresolved call. Notes include contradictory font-size arithmetic, so research statements are not accepted as verified facts.

Identifies Don Berg CHESS88 V2.0 and provides disassembly, Ghidra notes, MZ analysis and portable board/move/evaluation/search code. New beginner mode deliberately uses random legal moves. Candidate-move exclusion and one king-safety mode remain partially traced. Old notes call the original text-only while later sections discuss extracted bitmap glyphs; preserve this research evolution rather than claiming complete equivalence.

Original author remakes the 1998 Mission 2000 game, extending its object and level systems. README says nearly all maps were exported from Spectrum and supports Hobeta format; inspected Lua has its own object, player, inventory and world state rather than a Z80 execution core. New mechanics and editor make this an expanded remake.

Native ZX Spectrum 48K adaptation of Magical Drop II. Board, pattern, injection and blitter modules implement gameplay in Z80, with BeepFX audio. Author marks it work in progress despite playable claim.

Unity remake of Spectrum Blockus. Inspected block component handles rigidbody collision, vertical collection zones, prize cycling and animation with a GameManager. Source establishes active game mechanics but no original-code recovery or behaviour comparison.

Phaser implementation of C64 Nova and Nova 2 laser puzzles, with mirrors, splitters, timed blocks and Tiled level sources. Inspected LaserHead handles beam motion and grid alignment. Author explicitly disclaims accuracy/completeness; README lists an out-of-view laser termination bug and unfinished effects/progress UI.

Native ST course project with scrolling model, alien/player projectile collisions, VBL/IKBD handlers and PSG audio. Inspected model implements simplified score-triggered waves; full Defender rescue rules and original fidelity are not established.

Remake of the Trailblazer game family, explicitly based on the author's Commodore 16 experience. New solar-system tracks, own music and modern physics. Ball controller models jump, airborne, lost and won states; this is not restoration of the Amiga or C64 binary.

Native 128K CPC tactical-stealth demake inspired by Commandos: Behind Enemy Lines, with original missions and mechanics rather than original executable recovery. Inspected Z80 sight code calculates angles and distance, then samples fifteen intermediate points against opaque map tiles. Training and seven mission descriptions plus emulator scenario/fuzz tooling are present.
Big-box Action Replay III hardware recreation, not application/firmware source reconstruction.
Unreal university 3D reinterpretation. Main gameplay assets are binary Blueprints; source-level coverage and finished scope were not established from available text.
DOS Capstone/MZ/map-file analysis utility, not a reconstructed game/application. Useful adjacent tooling but not promoted in this game-focused pass.

Fork of already tracked kylofon/test-drive-sdl3. Simulation models register sets and dispatches assembly labels while retaining real-mode memory; do not add duplicate or assume a fully semantic rewrite from README.
Explicit fork of tracked kylofon Street Rod 2 with macOS setup changes. No separate project promotion without substantial distinct restoration.
General Ghidra rules pipeline demonstrated on modern crackmes; not a DOS game/application reconstruction despite search match.

Spectrum remake candidate with historical Windows C++ sources, but selected implementation blobs were not returned as readable UTF-8. Identity, completeness and build requirements need further source review.
Space Taxi remake page says author is still searching for source. Root has README/screenshots only; no recovered code to promote.
New Atari ST Flappy Bird-style course game with C/assembly, but not restoration of a legacy game/application; retain as adjacent demake lead.

source_updates.reason: Source-informed remake of Atari Turbo-BASIC Kaiser II with extracted rule references and separate original/remake rule sets. Inspected ruleset selector defaults to the changed remake rules unless the player explicitly selects Atari. Recreated UI/audio and bug interpretation prevent an unqualified fidelity claim.
Action Replay III hardware schematic/GAL/PCB recreation; outside this game/application software pass.
Early Python network/board skeleton. Inspected server imports absent thromolusng.crypto and has an undefined coll variable; no complete remake established.
Abandoned C++/Irrlicht remake attempt. Sparse README and CMake do not establish original gameplay coverage; needs deeper libleg inspection before promotion.
DOS Tapper RE root contains COM executable and IDA databases, but no inspectable textual recovered implementation. Database content not reviewed.
Course writeup identifies a life-counter address and short instruction sequence; no reconstructed game or substantial source. Screenshot placeholders remain.
Lords of Conquest browser prototype. Inspected client models/render countries/resources and random ownership changes; full turns/combat/economy reconstruction not established.
Same Pokitto Sensitive remake already tracked under Sensitive-without-lib-source. This root bundles platform library/history; avoid duplicate project.
LibGDX C64 oil-game learning project. Inspected turn logic remains simplistic and getNextYear increments twice; original game rules/completion not established.
Roland Goes Digging LibGDX remake declaration only; repository tree has README/license/gitignore, no implementation.
